name: James E. Risch
signature: Frames AI's electricity appetite as the case for an Idaho-led nuclear build-out; co-leads the TEST AI Act on federal AI safety testing.

notable_quote.text: this huge demand we’re going to have for power in just a very few years because of AI and these other things coming online, they realize that it is going to take nuclear power

data_centers.summary: Risch treats AI-driven electricity demand as real and answers it with more nuclear power, including his 2026 ARC Act to help finance new reactors. No statements found on data center siting, ratepayer costs, or the Meta Kuna project as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Risch touts significance of nuclear energy to growing energy demand (Senate Energy hearing remarks)
evidence.what_it_shows: At a July 2025 Senate Energy hearing he said he had been a doubter about forecasts of AI-driven electricity demand but now expects the country to be inundated with demand, and that nuclear power is how to meet it.

evidence.title: KMVT: Idaho leaders push for nuclear energy expansion with new task force, federal bill
evidence.quote: this huge demand we’re going to have for power in just a very few years because of AI and these other things coming online, they realize that it is going to take nuclear power
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties AI and data center power demand directly to his bipartisan Accelerating Reliable Capacity (ARC) Act, which would put $3.6 billion behind finishing new commercial reactors.

ai_risk.summary: His only AI-specific action is co-leading the TEST AI Act, which has the national labs and NIST build test beds to check whether AI systems are safe and trustworthy. It funds testing rather than rules, so it does not show a clear lean toward or against regulation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1633 TEST AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-led a bipartisan bill directing the Energy Department and NIST to build test beds for measuring whether AI systems are safe and reliable.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3162 TEST AI Act of 2024 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the earlier version of the same AI testing bill, showing a sustained interest in federal AI evaluation capacity.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Bipartisan Senate bill looks to improve AI testing
evidence.what_it_shows: Names Risch as one of five senators introducing the TEST AI Act; the article carries a quote from Sen. Lujan on AI vulnerabilities and risks but no Risch quote.

tech_regulation.summary: Backs targeted rules for online platforms: he cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act and the STOP CSAM Act and has long pushed against TikTok's Chinese ownership. No support found for Big Tech break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring social media and gaming platforms to build in safety tools for minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making platforms do more to report and remove child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1409 Kids Online Safety Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed KOSA in the prior Congress too, a consistent kids' safety position.

evidence.title: KTVB: Idaho delegates vote on TikTok ban bill (Risch office statement)
evidence.quote: Senator Risch has long voiced concerns about TikTok given the CCP's ability to control the app.
evidence.what_it_shows: His communications director said he leaned toward the TikTok divest-or-ban bill and had written the FTC in 2023 about the app's influence on children.

preemption.summary: Voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the 2025 budget bill, but that near-unanimous vote came after the deal collapsed and is not a stated position. No statements, letters, or bills on preemption found as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium; because nearly every senator voted the same way, this alone does not show where he stands on preemption.

china_chips.summary: He signed a July 2026 letter pressing Apple not to buy memory chips from Chinese military-linked companies and has long attacked China's theft of Micron's technology. No statement found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales to China or on the Chip Security Act.

evidence.title: MacRumors: Senators demand Apple commit to not buying Chinese memory chips (Risch a signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined Sen. Schumer's bipartisan letter asking Apple to commit not to use memory chips from China's CXMT or YMTC, a hawkish, Micron-friendly stance on Chinese chipmakers.

evidence.title: Press release: In hearing on worldwide threats, Risch points to Micron as example of technology, IP theft by China
evidence.what_it_shows: At a Senate Intelligence hearing he called China the real concern and used Chinese theft of Micron's memory chip technology as his prime example of why China must live by rule of law.

evidence.title: Press release: Crapo, Risch, Simpson, Fulcher support inclusion of chips permitting reform in defense bill
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a 115-lawmaker letter to keep NEPA permitting relief for U.S. semiconductor plants in the FY24 defense bill; this is about building chips at home, not export controls.

name: Mike Crapo
signature: Senate Finance chairman who wants Congress to understand AI before regulating it, while pressing agencies on AI safeguards in Social Security and Medicare.

notable_quote.text: To mitigate the risks associated with deploying AI across its programs, SSA must have strong governance frameworks in place that, among other important aspects, clarify the role of human discretion.

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on data centers, Idaho Power's large-load rates, or the Meta Kuna project as of Sept 2026. Searches of his press releases and Idaho news coverage turned up nothing on the topic.

ai_risk.summary: Leans light touch: he told a 2024 Finance hearing that Congress should understand how AI works before legislating and warned that rigid one-size-fits-all rules could stifle medical advances, and in 2026 he defended Medicare's AI-assisted prior authorization pilot. He does back oversight of AI in government benefit decisions, pressing Social Security on AI safeguards in 2024.

evidence.title: Press release: Crapo statement at Finance hearing on AI in health care
evidence.what_it_shows: As Finance ranking member he said Congress should not legislate first and ask questions later, called one-size-fits-all AI rules a risk to life-saving advances, and favored a sector-specific, risk-based approach with targeted oversight of algorithms that improperly deny care.

name: Russ Fulcher
signature: Former Micron employee on Energy and Commerce who grills witnesses on AI chatbots and kids and on AI bioterror risks, and pushes geothermal to power AI demand.
groups: Vice Chair, House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade
Member, House Republican Big Tech Censorship and Data Task Force (2021)

notable_quote.text: Kids are wired to form attachments with things that act friendly. What we don’t want happening is a chatbot taking the role of teaching a child right and wrong.

data_centers.summary: Supports building more power supply to meet AI-driven demand, mainly through faster permitting of geothermal on federal land, and frames it as a way to keep consumer prices low. He sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee that advanced the Ratepayer Protection Act 52-0 in July 2026, but his individual vote and any statement on it were not found.

evidence.title: Press release: Fulcher introduces bill to unleash power of geothermal energy and lower costs (H.R. 5576)
evidence.quote: This clean, abundant resource has the potential to help meet the United States’ power demand, which is increasing at a historic rate due in part to AI and other technological advancements.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI-driven demand as a reason to cut federal red tape and build more generation, with lower consumer prices as the stated goal.

evidence.title: Op-ed: Geothermal, the energy powerhouse Idaho already understands
evidence.quote: Ensuring America is ready to meet these growing needs through various power sources, such as geothermal, is essential to keeping prices low for consumers and strengthening our energy independence.
evidence.what_it_shows: He links rising electricity demand driven in part by AI to the need for new supply and permitting reform, while naming consumer prices as the concern.

ai_risk.summary: Mixed. He cheers AI as a field where America must lead and praised the 2025 House package that promoted AI, but he presses hard on specific harms: kids forming attachments to chatbots, AI-faked sexual images, AI-enabled bioweapons and terrorism. No support found for broad AI licensing or safety mandates.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing on AI chatbots: Fulcher questions on kids and chatbots
evidence.quote: Kids are wired to form attachments with things that act friendly. What we don’t want happening is a chatbot taking the role of teaching a child right and wrong.
evidence.what_it_shows: He worries children will treat chatbots as parental authorities and, per the hearing transcript, that customizable chatbots can validate abusers and pull struggling users away from human relationships.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.633 TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports criminalizing AI-faked sexual images and forcing fast takedowns, a targeted AI harm rule now law.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.6499 Assessing Safety Tools for Parents and Minors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill orders a study of parental control tools; it was part of the 18-bill kids' online safety package the E&C subcommittee advanced in December 2025.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing on AI and biotechnology: Fulcher on stopping AI-enabled bio threats
evidence.quote: can you say what specific parts of that order are actually going to stop these threats, or have the best chance of stopping these threats?
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked whether the May 2025 executive order's gene synthesis screening provisions would stop AI-enabled biological threats and what more Congress should do.

evidence.title: Fulcher video: 'Are we at that point?' Fulcher questions if terrorists can use AI to carry out attacks
evidence.what_it_shows: Video-only post of his hearing questions on whether terrorists can already use AI to carry out attacks; shows attention to catastrophic misuse, direction on rules unclear.

evidence.title: Press release: Fulcher on Energy and Commerce passage of reconciliation text
evidence.quote: This legislation takes important steps to strengthen America’s leadership on the world stage by supporting rapid technological advancements in Artificial Intelligence
evidence.what_it_shows: He framed AI as a race for American leadership and praised the committee text that promoted AI adoption, a pro-innovation counterweight to his harm-focused questioning.

tech_regulation.summary: Backs targeted tech rules rather than break-ups: his bill making smart appliances disclose hidden cameras and microphones passed the House in 2025, he cosponsors kids' online safety and car-data privacy bills, voted for the TikTok divest-or-ban bill, and served on the 2021 House GOP Big Tech task force calling to rein in the companies' power.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.859 Informing Consumers about Smart Devices Act

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.6734 Auto Data Privacy and Autonomy Act

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.7891 Kids Online Safety Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the House KOSA requiring platforms to protect kids from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.7890 Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (118th Congress)

evidence.what_it_shows: On joining the GOP Big Tech Censorship and Data task force he called for reining in Big Tech over speech bans and data practices.

evidence.quote: This bipartisan bill provides Americans with an additional tool to protect their private information.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would force websites and apps owned by the Chinese Communist Party to disclose that ownership to users.

evidence.title: KTVB: Idaho delegates vote on TikTok ban bill
evidence.what_it_shows: KTVB reports he voted yea on the House bill forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to divest or face a ban.
